Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Not recorded, DOB: Not recorded, Gender: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Doctor Smith, Practice: Babylon, Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Persistent severe headache (3 days) with photophobia and visual phenomena — provisional primary headache disorder (probable migraine) consistent with transcript and DDx.
- Secondary: Functional impairment — difficulty concentrating and reduced ability to work from home due to headache.
- Tertiary: Possible concern for secondary neurological causes (DDx considerations) — cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST), idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) — medium likelihood per DDx; subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) lower likelihood per DDx.
(DDx from diagnostic reasoning model included where consistent with transcript.)

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (name not documented; started ~1 year ago; dose/route/frequency not documented). Ibuprofen taken intermittently for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented). Clinician advised paracetamol may be taken concurrently. Clinician stated intention to prescribe a stronger analgesic (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies/ADRs: No allergies reported.
- Past Medical History: Occasional mild, short-lived headaches in childhood/younger years; otherwise none recorded.

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Not recorded.
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): Not recorded.
- Family History: Mother with severe migraines (reports of vomiting with her migraines).

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives alone.
- Social Support: Not recorded.
- Occupation/Education: Works from home.
- Alcohol Use: Drinks alcohol approximately once weekly ("three, once a week" reported).
- Smoking/Substance Use: Does not smoke. No recreational drug use reported.
- Key Stressors: Persistent severe headache causing inability to concentrate and missed work days.

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Not recorded.
- Mood & Affect: Not recorded.
- Speech & Thought: Not recorded.
- Perception: Reports photophobia and intermittent visual phenomena described as "shooting lights" (subjective visual disturbance).

Cognition:
- Orientation: Not recorded.
- Attention/Concentration: Reports decreased ability to focus; difficulty completing work tasks.
- Memory: Not recorded.
- Insight & Judgement: Patient recognizes severity of symptoms and has sought medical assessment; willing to attend further examination.

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Sleeping well; headache may be present on waking but not waking patient from sleep.
- Appetite: No change reported.
- Motivation/Energy: Reports some lack of energy, attributed to ongoing headache.
- Anxiety Symptoms: Not recorded.

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: No suicidal ideation, self-harm, or risk to others reported.
- Protective Factors: Engaged with care, seeks assessment; retains sleep; has prior eye check reportedly normal.
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low (based on no self-harm ideation or intent reported).
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded.

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Family history of migraine (mother), female on combined oral contraceptive pill.
- Precipitating factors: Sudden onset of severe headache on waking 3 days ago.
- Perpetuating factors: Ongoing severe pain with incomplete relief from OTC analgesia leading to reduced concentration and functional impairment; delayed in-person neurological/exam diagnostics.
- Protective factors: Patient engaged with clinician, sleeping adequately, no systemic features (no fever, no vomiting), no focal neurological deficits reported to date.
- Integrative summary: Presentation most consistent with probable migraine with visual phenomena (high likelihood per DDx). However, given combined OCP use and subacute persistent severe headache with visual disturbance, secondary neurological causes (CVST, IIH) are reasonable considerations; clinician recommended urgent face-to-face neurological exam and fundoscopy and advised A&E if symptoms worsen.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Obtain diagnosis and effective symptom relief; return to usual work functioning; avoid serious complications.
- Clinical Goal(s): Complete timely neurological examination including fundoscopy and blood pressure check; exclude secondary causes (e.g., CVST, IIH, SAH) as indicated; initiate appropriate analgesic/acute headache management; review suitability of combined OCP if migraine with aura is confirmed.
- Actions (Patient): Book and attend the face-to-face appointment with support team for full neurological exam and fundoscopy; take prescribed analgesia as directed (medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented); take paracetamol concurrently if advised; monitor symptoms and go to A&E if headache becomes unbearable, changes character, or is associated with vomiting, reduced consciousness, focal deficits, or other red flags.
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange urgent face-to-face neurological assessment and fundoscopy; check blood pressure at appointment; prescribe stronger analgesic (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) and advise paracetamol may be taken concurrently; consider neuroimaging and/or urgent referral (e.g., emergency imaging or neurology) if red flags or examination findings warrant; advise on OCP review if migraine with aura is confirmed.

Secondary Problem (Functional impairment: reduced concentration and work capacity):
- Patient Goal(s): Improve concentration and resume work responsibilities.
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce headache frequency/intensity and improve functional capacity.
- Actions (Patient): Adhere to prescribed acute symptom management; minimize exposure to bright lights and other triggers; rest as needed and pace activities until symptoms improve.
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide follow-up review after neurological assessment to reassess functional status and work capacity; provide further advice/support as indicated (sick leave documentation not recorded).

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: probable migraine vs possible secondary causes; need for neurological examination and fundoscopy; take prescribed medication with food; when to attend A&E (headache worsening, change in pattern, vomiting, decreased consciousness, focal neurological signs); potential need to review combined OCP if migraine aura confirmed.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing severity or change in headache character, persistent or new vomiting, fever, focal neurological deficits (weakness, numbness, slurred speech), loss of consciousness, visual loss — attend A&E if these occur.
- Coping Strategies: Rest in a dark/quiet environment, avoid bright lights, use prescribed analgesia as directed, maintain sleep hygiene, seek prompt assessment if not improving.

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Patient agreed to book appointment and proceed with examination (verbal agreement recorded).
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded.
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded.
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded.
- Review Date: Not recorded (review pending at face-to-face appointment/support team evaluation).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine (probable migraine with visual aura) — Likelihood: High. Justification: Photophobia, subjective visual phenomena ("shooting lights"), severe pain (8/10) partially responsive to ibuprofen, family history of migraine; no fever or focal deficits.
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — Likelihood: Medium. Justification: Young woman on combined OCP (increased thrombotic risk) with subacute progressive headache and visual symptoms; positional/exertional element reported; requires exclusion with imaging if exam concerning.
- Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) — Likelihood: Medium. Justification: Young woman with persistent headache and transient visual disturbances; fundoscopy for papilledema and further evaluation required to exclude.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Patient identifying details (name, DOB, contact, address); formal vital signs; neurological examination findings; fundoscopy results; imaging/laboratory results; explicit mental health history and MSE details (mood/affect, appearance, speech) — these are not recorded in the transcript. Treatment details for prescribed analgesic and contraceptive specifics (name/dose) are not documented.
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None significant — DDx and transcript are largely consistent (both favor migraine while recommending exclusion of secondary causes). No conflicts noted. 
● Transcript quality notes: Several patient identifiers were not provided/confirmed in the transcript. Some patient statements were fragmented; clinical assessment planning (prescription specifics, appointment scheduling) referenced but medication name/dose and appointment date/time not documented.
